claims.text: The target system is an FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix.
A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can be introduced into the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Introducing this architecture can improve the coating's overall wear resistance relative to an unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The intervention will remain beneficial across varied thermal regimes.
The intervention will remain beneficial across varied contact regimes.
The nanohierarchical architecture provides multi-type adaptive friction-interface protection.
The adaptive interface protection is governed by intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The proposed wear-resistance benefit should hold from room temperature to 800 °C.
The exact mechanism by which the architecture improves wear resistance is not fully understood.
Wear rate and friction coefficient can be measured in sliding tests over varied thermal and contact regimes.
The modified coating is predicted to have a significantly lower wear rate than the unchanged coating.

contradictions.description: The mechanism field names a specific governing mechanism involving adaptive interface protection, nano-coupled grains, and nanoprecipitates, while the uncertainty field says the exact mechanism is not fully understood. This is a tension between a specific mechanistic assertion and the stated uncertainty.
